\documentclass[11pt]{article}
\usepackage{amsmath,amssymb}
\usepackage[margin=1in]{geometry}
\usepackage{microtype}
\setlength{\parskip}{0pt}
\title{Rewritten Chain of Thought for the Closed-Form $A_n$\\ in the Two-Minus Water-Wave Sector}
\date{}
\begin{document}
\maketitle

\begin{abstract}
\noindent This document is a rewritten, first-person summary of the chain of thought I followed while
looking for a closed form for the tree-level on-shell amplitude $A_n$ of $1$D deep-water surface waves
in the two-minus sector $\sigma=(-1,-1,+1,\dots,+1)$, working only from the prompt and the
Berends--Giele code \texttt{OnShellBG.m}. It keeps the dead ends and the reconsiderations, because the
shape of the answer only became clear through them.
\end{abstract}

\section*{Rewritten Chain of Thought}

The dispersion is $\omega_i^2=g\,|k_i|$, so each momentum is fixed by its frequency up to a sign,
$k_i=\sigma_i\,\omega_i^2/g$, and on the resonant manifold
$$\sum_i \omega_i = 0,\qquad \sum_i \sigma_i\,\omega_i^2 = 0,$$
the second of which is just momentum conservation $\sum_i k_i=0$. The two minus legs are legs $1,2$.
The hint promises a single global rational function $A_n=N(\omega)/D(\omega)$, with $D$ the product of
the channel factors and simple poles on the factorization channels, and it insists: no piecewise
decomposition, no absolute values, no $\min/\max$, and \emph{not} a plain polynomial. I will take that
as a working hypothesis but I will trust whatever \texttt{BGAmplitude} actually returns over the hint.

My first move is purely mechanical: I want to evaluate the amplitude fast and exactly, because the
Mathematica recursion is slow and I will need hundreds of points. I re-typed the kernel/vertex/%
propagator/recursion definitions and ported them to exact Gaussian-rational Python. The first port was
wrong by large factors; comparing kernels term by term against Mathematica localised it to
$\mathrm{FKernel}[n\ge4]$, whose Mathematica definition divides the \emph{entire} accumulated result by
$|p_2|$ at the end. After restoring that final $/\,|p_2|$ the port reproduces \texttt{BGAmplitude}
exactly: $A_5=-2304\,i$ at $\{2,5/2,3\}$, $A_5=-\tfrac{404919}{905}i$, $A_6=-\tfrac{11907}{4}i$, and so
on. Good---now I have ground truth on tap.

The kinematic solver wants $\sigma_1+\sigma_n=0$, which holds here since $\sigma_1=-1,\sigma_n=+1$, so it
solves linearly for $\{\omega_1,\omega_n\}$ given $n-2$ free frequencies. Running it I immediately hit a
surprise at $n=4$: \texttt{BGAmplitude} returns \texttt{Indeterminate}. Solving the two conservation
laws for $n=4$ by hand shows why---the solution set is rigid,
$$\{\omega_1,\omega_2\}=\{-\omega_3,-\omega_4\},\qquad \text{i.e. } \omega=(-b,\,a,\,b,\,-a),$$
so the two-particle sub-channels $\{1,3\}$ and $\{2,4\}$ have $\omega_S=0$ and $k_S=0$
\emph{simultaneously}, and the propagator $-i/(\omega_S^2/|k_S|-g)$ is a literal $0/0$. So $n=4$ sits
exactly on a factorization boundary; I will have to treat it as a limit and come back to it.

Scaling all $\omega\to\lambda\omega$ shows $A_n\to\lambda^{2(n-2)}A_n$ (measured $\lambda^6,\lambda^8,
\lambda^{10}$ at $n=5,6,7$), so $A_n$ is homogeneous of degree $2(n-2)$, and it is purely imaginary.

Now the structure. The conservation laws give, for the two minus legs in terms of the plus frequencies
$x=(\omega_3,\dots,\omega_n)$,
$$\omega_1+\omega_2=-e_1(x),\qquad \omega_1\omega_2=e_2(x),\qquad \omega_1^2+\omega_2^2=\textstyle\sum_{j\ge3}\omega_j^2,$$
which I checked numerically. Since legs $1,2$ are identical and legs $3,\dots,n$ are identical, $A_n$ is
symmetric under $S_2\times S_{n-2}$; being symmetric in $\omega_1,\omega_2$ it depends on them only
through $e_1(x),e_2(x)$, hence \emph{$A_n$ should be a symmetric rational function of the plus
frequencies alone}. That is a big simplification, and it tells me the channel factors. For an all-plus
subset $S$ the internal momentum $k_S=\sum_{i\in S}\omega_i^2>0$ identically, so $|k_S|=k_S$ and the
propagator factor is honestly polynomial,
$$\omega_S^2-k_S=2\!\!\sum_{i<j\in S}\!\omega_i\omega_j=2\,e_2(x_S),$$
with no absolute value; whereas a type-1 subset (one minus leg $\mu$ plus some plus legs $P$) has
$k_S=-\omega_\mu^2+\sum_{j\in P}\omega_j^2$ of indefinite sign, so $\omega_S^2-|k_S|$ carries a genuine
$|\cdot|$ that does not collapse to one polynomial. The hint says ``no absolute values,'' so I
conjecture the denominator is built only from all-plus channels and try to fit $N$.

This fails. With $D$ a product of $e_2(x_S)$ factors and $N$ a generic symmetric polynomial of the
matching degree, no fit is consistent---at any of the candidate denominators. So I drop the assumed
denominator and reconstruct $A_5=N/D$ with $N,D$ \emph{both} general symmetric polynomials, solving the
homogeneous system $A\cdot D-N=0$ over a few hundred exact points and reading off the null space. For
every denominator degree up to $12$ the null space is empty. I sanity-check the solver on a synthetic
symmetric rational function and it recovers it instantly, so the solver is fine. The conclusion is
uncomfortable: either $A_5$ is rational of denominator degree larger than anything reasonable, or it is
\emph{not} a rational function of the plus frequencies at all.

To see what is going on I reconstruct $A_5$ along a one-parameter slice, fixing $\omega_2=2,\omega_3=5/2$
and varying $\omega_4=t$ with $\omega_5,\omega_1$ derived. Exact rational interpolation gives
$$A_5(t)=-\,256\,\frac{4t^2+18t+45}{2t+9}.$$
The only pole, at $t=-9/2$, is where $\omega_2+\omega_3+\omega_4=0$, i.e. where $\omega_5\to\infty$---a
parametrization artifact, not a physical channel. So along this slice $A_5$ has \emph{no} physical pole.
Even stranger, computing $e_2(x)$ along the same slice gives $-(4t^2+18t+45)/(2t+9)$ exactly, so
$$A_5(t)=256\,e_2(x)=256\,\omega_1\omega_2 \qquad\text{(on this slice).}$$
But $A_5$ is degree $6$ and $\omega_1\omega_2$ is degree $2$, so the ``$256$'' cannot be a constant; it
must hide a degree-$4$ quantity that happens to be $256$ here.

So I look at $G:=A_5/(\omega_1\omega_2)$, a degree-$4$ symmetric object, over many points. It equals
$256$ at a great many configurations---but $207$, $112$, $\dots$ at others. A degree-$4$ homogeneous
function cannot be constant on an open set unless it is globally constant, so the points where $G=256$
cannot form an open set: there is a wall. Tabulating, $G$ is always a perfect fourth power on one side,
$$256=4^4,\quad 625=5^4,\quad 1296=6^4,\quad 2401=7^4,\quad 4096=8^4,$$
with base $2\,\omega_{\min}$ where $\omega_{\min}$ is the smallest-magnitude leg---but only when that leg
is one of the minus legs. The deviations $207,112,\dots$ appear exactly when a plus leg becomes the
softest, and the transition is governed by $\operatorname{sign}(k_{24})=\operatorname{sign}(\omega_4^2-\omega_2^2)$. This is a chamber
structure, driven by the $|k_S|$ in the propagators.

I tried to localise it: group points by the sign pattern of all composite $k_S=\sum_{i\in S}\sigma_i\omega_i^2$ and
reconstruct within a single chamber. The symmetric reconstruction still fails inside one chamber, and
the reason is subtle but decisive: a chamber is not invariant under $S_2\times S_{n-2}$ (it is defined by
inequalities like $\omega_4^2\gtrless\omega_2^2$ that single out legs), so the per-chamber expression need
\emph{not} be symmetric in the plus frequencies even though the physical value is. My plus-frequency
ansatz was therefore the wrong object on a single chamber. I confirmed the symmetry of the physical
amplitude directly---swapping $\omega_1\leftrightarrow\omega_2$, and permuting plus legs, leaves
\texttt{BGAmplitude} unchanged---so the amplitude is a genuine $S_2\times S_{n-2}$ function; it is just
not a single rational one.

At this point I worried this contradicts the hint, so I cross-checked the ``deviation'' values against
the reference Mathematica itself: $A_5=-\tfrac{5589}{4}i$ at $\{2,5/2,3/2\}$, $-\tfrac{7504}{11}i$ at
$\{2,5/2,1\}$. The reference code reproduces them. The piecewise behaviour is real, and it is exactly
what the comment in \texttt{OnShellBG.m} hints at when it says ``no poles in this sector'': the
propagator poles cancel in the full sum, leaving a \emph{bounded} amplitude whose only non-analyticity is
the $|k_S|$. A scan confirms $|A_5|/(\text{scale})^{6}\lesssim 3$ everywhere; there are no real poles.

Is it actually discontinuous, or merely kinked? Refining the one-sided derivatives across the wall
$\omega_4=\omega_2$ with smaller steps, the two slopes converge, so the amplitude is continuous and very
nearly smooth at the wall. That briefly reopened the single-rational hope, so I tested the cleanest
candidate hard: on increasing-ordered positive free frequencies (where $\omega_2$ is the global
softest),
$$A_5=16\,\omega_1\,\omega_2^5$$
holds at $84/84$ grid points and continues to hold at deliberately generic, near-equal-magnitude
increasing points. That is the killer. If $A_5$ equalled the polynomial $16\,\omega_1\omega_2^5$ on an
open set and were a single rational function, it would equal it everywhere; but at $\{2,5/2,3/2\}$ it is
$-\tfrac{5589}{4}i\neq 16\,\omega_1\omega_2^5$. Sharper still, within the region where the softest leg is
a minus leg, on the open piece $\{\omega_1^2<\omega_2^2\}$ the amplitude is the rational function
$16\,\omega_1^5\omega_2$, while on $\{\omega_2^2<\omega_1^2\}$ it is the \emph{different} rational
function $16\,\omega_1\omega_2^5$ (verified $67/67$ and $233/233$). No single rational function can equal
two different ones on two open sets. So the hint's premise is, for this code, false: $A_n$ is bounded and
piecewise, not a single rational function.

That ``$16\,\omega_1\omega_2^5$'' is too clean to be a coincidence, though, and it generalises. The
prefactor is $2^{n-1}$ ($16$ at $n=5$, $32$ at $n=6$), and the symmetric form, using
$\min(\omega_1^2,\omega_2^2)$ for the softer minus leg, is
$$\boxed{\,A_n = i\,2^{\,n-1}\,\omega_1\omega_2\,\bigl(\min(\omega_1^2,\omega_2^2)\bigr)^{n-3}\,}\qquad
\text{whenever }\min_i\omega_i^2\text{ is a }\sigma=-1\text{ leg.}$$
This is sign-robust (it holds for arbitrary signs of the frequencies, not just the increasing-positive
slice), and it reproduces \texttt{BGAmplitude} exactly: $112/112$ at $n=5$, $420/420$ at $n=6$, and on
random-sign points $200/200,\,40/40,\,8/8$ at $n=5,6,7$ with zero mismatches; it never holds when a plus
leg is the softest. Notably, this principal regime contains every two-minus example in
\texttt{OnShellBG.m}, where positive comparable free frequencies always make a minus leg the softest.

For $n=4$ the same formula reads $A_4=i\,8\,\omega_1\omega_2\min(\omega_1^2,\omega_2^2)$, and although
\texttt{BGAmplitude} is the degenerate $0/0$ there, approaching the rigid manifold from off-shell,
$\omega\to(-b,a,b+\varepsilon,-a+\varepsilon)$ with $\varepsilon\to0$, the limit converges to it:
$-192,-1080,-320,-864$ for $(a,b)=(2,3),(3,5),(2,5),(4,3)$.

But ``softest is a minus leg'' is a minority of generic configurations once $n\ge5$ (there are $n-2$ plus
legs against two minus legs), so I need the rest of the sector. The clean power form breaks there:
$A_5/(\omega_1\omega_2)$ is no longer a perfect square, and a symmetric reconstruction restricted to the
plus-softest region also fails because that region is itself cut into finer chambers by the remaining
$k_S$ signs. The honest variables are the type-1 channel momenta themselves. So I posit a single global
ansatz that allows the absolute values explicitly:
$$A_5 = i\Bigl[\,P_0(\omega)\;+\!\!\sum_{\mu\in\{1,2\}}\sum_{j\in\{3,4,5\}}\!\!P_{\mu j}(\omega)\,\bigl|\omega_j^2-\omega_\mu^2\bigr|\Bigr],$$
with $P_0$ symmetric of degree $6$ and the coefficient family symmetric under the residual symmetry. The
$|\omega_j^2-\omega_\mu^2|=|k_{\mu j}|$ are exactly the type-1 (one minus, one plus) channel momenta.
Fitting this is now a \emph{single linear} problem across all chambers; the augmented system is
rank-deficient only because of the manifold relations, but it is \emph{consistent}---a single $P_0$ and a
single family $P_{\mu j}$ reproduce every chamber. One exact representative is
$$P_0=8\,\omega_1\omega_2\,(P_4-4E_1E_3),\quad P_4=\omega_3^4+\omega_4^4+\omega_5^4,$$
with $E_1,E_3$ the elementary symmetric functions of the plus legs, and
$$P_{\mu j}=8\bigl(e_1^3\omega_{\mu'}+2e_1e_2\,\omega_j-e_1e_2\,\omega_{\mu'}-e_1\omega_{\mu'}^3+2e_2^2+e_2\omega_{\mu'}^2\bigr),$$
where $\mu'$ is the other minus leg and $e_1,e_2$ are the elementary symmetric functions of the two plus
legs other than $j$. This complete $n=5$ form matches \texttt{BGAmplitude} at $800$ random points
spanning all chambers (the softest leg observed to be each of the five legs in turn), with zero
mismatches. So the absolute values the hint forbade are in fact essential and unavoidable; they are how
the chamber structure enters, and once they are admitted the amplitude \emph{is} a single global
expression.

I then asked whether the same linear-in-$|k|$ ansatz works for $n=6$. It does not---it is inconsistent.
The resolution is that $n=6$ needs \emph{products} of $|k_S|$ (the formula is multilinear in the type-1
momenta), reflecting the $n-3$ nested soft channels, with $n=5$ being the lucky case that needs only a
single factor. The clean limits survive across $n$ and corroborate this picture: when the $n-3$ softest
legs are all $\sigma=+1$ I find
$$A_n = i\,2^{\,n-1}(n-3)!\,\omega_1\omega_2\!\!\prod_{\text{softest }n-3\text{ plus}}\!\!\omega_j^2,$$
the factorial coefficient being the signature of a sum over the orderings of the soft channels, while
the soft-minus end gives the $(\min(\omega_1^2,\omega_2^2))^{n-3}$ above. I did not extract the full set
of multilinear coefficients for $n\ge6$; that is the one piece I leave as the explicit
$n=5$ form plus these general-$n$ boundary laws and the structural statement.

The physics that ties it together: in this sector the would-be propagator poles
$\omega_S^2=|k_S|$ never produce a pole of the assembled amplitude---they cancel---so $A_n$ is bounded
and equals, on each chamber, a polynomial of degree $2(n-2)$ in the frequencies. The chambers are the
sign patterns of the type-1 sub-energies $k_S=\sum_{i\in S}\sigma_i\omega_i^2$; the all-plus channels are
always positive and contribute nothing piecewise. The amplitude is dominated by the softest legs, with
the softest minus leg acting as a cap (giving the clean power law) and soft plus legs contributing the
nested $|k_{\mu j}|$ structure. Everything I claim is checked to the last digit in exact rational
arithmetic against the supplied \texttt{BGAmplitude}; where I could not produce a clean general-$n$
formula I say so rather than dress up the $n=5$ result as more than it is.

\end{document}

\documentclass[11pt]{article}
\usepackage{amsmath,amssymb}
\usepackage[margin=1in]{geometry}
\usepackage{microtype}
\setlength{\parskip}{2pt}
\newcommand{\bg}{\texttt{BGAmplitude}}
\title{Rewritten Chain of Thought for the Closed-Form $A_n$\\ in the Two-Minus Water-Wave Sector\\[4pt]
\large (detailed, chronological)}
\date{}
\begin{document}
\maketitle

\begin{abstract}
\noindent A first-person, blow-by-blow record of the chain of thought I followed while searching for a
closed form for the tree-level on-shell amplitude $A_n$ of $1$D deep-water surface waves in the
two-minus sector $\sigma=(-1,-1,+1,\dots,+1)$, working only from the prompt and the Berends--Giele code
\texttt{OnShellBG.m}. Every hypothesis, every numerical example, every dead end and every fix is kept,
in the order it actually happened.
\end{abstract}

\section*{0. Reading the problem}
The dispersion is $\omega_i^2=g\,|k_i|$, so $k_i=\sigma_i\,\omega_i^2/g$ with $\sigma_i=\pm1$, and on the
resonant manifold
$$\sum_i\omega_i=0,\qquad \sum_i\sigma_i\,\omega_i^2=0$$
(the latter is $\sum_i k_i=0$). The two minus legs are legs $1,2$. The hint says $A_n=N(\omega)/D(\omega)$
is a single global rational function, $D$ a product of factorization-channel factors with simple poles,
\emph{no} chambers/absolute-values/$\min$/$\max$, and not a plain polynomial; fit $N$ by matching \bg{} at
a few hundred points. I decide to take that as a target but to trust whatever the code actually returns.
The constraints: I may read only \texttt{prompt.md} and \texttt{OnShellBG.m}, no web, but I may write and
run my own code. Environment: \texttt{wolframscript}, an Anaconda Python with \texttt{sympy}/\texttt{mpmath}.

\section*{1. Ground truth from the supplied code}
I re-typed the definitions into \texttt{bg\_defs.m} and wrote a driver that computes two-minus amplitudes
via \texttt{MakeKinematics}+\bg{}. The first results:
\begin{align*}
n=4,\ \{2,3\}:&\quad \omega=(-3,2,3,-2),\ \ A=\texttt{Indeterminate}\ (0/0);\\
n=4,\ \{5/2,7/3\}:&\quad A=\texttt{Indeterminate};\\
n=5,\ \{2,5/2,3\}:&\quad \omega=(-\tfrac92,2,\tfrac52,3,-3),\ \ A=-2304\,i;\\
n=5,\ \{3/2,11/5,7/3\}:&\quad A=-\tfrac{404919}{905}\,i;\\
n=6,\ \{3/2,2,5/2,3\}:&\quad A=-\tfrac{11907}{4}\,i;\\
n=6,\ \{2,3,7/2,11/3\}:&\quad A=-\tfrac{6588416}{219}\,i.
\end{align*}
The $n=4$ \texttt{Indeterminate} is not noise. Solving the two conservation laws at $n=4$ shows the
solution set is rigid: $\{\omega_1,\omega_2\}=\{-\omega_3,-\omega_4\}$, i.e. $\omega=(-b,a,b,-a)$. Then the
two-particle sub-channels $\{1,3\}$ and $\{2,4\}$ have $\omega_S=0$ \emph{and} $k_S=0$ at once, so the
propagator $-i/(\omega_S^2/|k_S|-g)$ is a literal $0/0$. So $n=4$ sits on a factorization boundary; I set
it aside as a limiting case.

\section*{2. A fast exact evaluator, and a bug}
I ported the whole recursion to exact Gaussian-rational Python (\texttt{bg.py}). First validation: at
$\{2,5/2,3\}$ it returned $+27907\,i$ instead of $-2304\,i$---off by a large factor, so a real bug. I
probed kernel by kernel against Mathematica on the $n=5$ momenta $k=(-\tfrac{81}{4},-4,\tfrac{25}{4},9,9)$:
\begin{align*}
\text{EKernel: } & -81,\ -162,\ -216 \ \ \text{(match)};\\
\text{FKernel}_3=-2\ \text{(match)};\quad
\text{FKernel}_4:&\ \text{Math }{-4},\ \text{Py }{-16};\qquad
\text{FKernel}_5:\ \text{Math }{-\tfrac{16}{3}},\ \text{Py }{-\tfrac{64}{3}}.
\end{align*}
So $\mathrm{FKernel}[n\ge4]$ was wrong by exactly the factor $|p_2|$. The Mathematica definition divides
the \emph{whole} accumulated result by $|p_2|$ at the very end; my port had dropped that final
$/\,|p_2|$. After restoring it the port reproduces \bg{} exactly:
$$-2304,\ -\tfrac{404919}{905},\ -\tfrac{11907}{4},\ -\tfrac{6588416}{219}.$$
Now I have ground truth on tap, fast and exact.

\section*{3. Homogeneity and the minus-leg identities}
Scaling free$\to2\cdot$free:
$$n=5:\ \tfrac{-147456}{-2304}=64=2^6,\quad n=6:\ 256=2^8,\quad n=7:\ 1024=2^{10},$$
so $A_n$ is homogeneous of degree $2(n-2)$ and purely imaginary. (Timing: $n=7\approx5.6$\,s/eval.)

Using conservation, the two minus legs obey, with $x=(\omega_3,\dots,\omega_n)$ the plus frequencies,
$$\omega_1+\omega_2=-e_1(x),\qquad \omega_1\omega_2=e_2(x),\qquad \omega_1^2+\omega_2^2=\textstyle\sum_{j\ge3}\omega_j^2.$$
Checked on the $n=5$ point $x=(\tfrac52,3,-3)$: $e_1=\tfrac52$ and $\omega_1+\omega_2=-\tfrac52$;
$e_2=-9$ and $\omega_1\omega_2=-9$. Since $A_n$ is symmetric under $S_2\times S_{n-2}$ and symmetric in
$\omega_1,\omega_2$, it depends on them only through $e_1,e_2$---so I expect $A_n$ to be a symmetric
rational function of the plus frequencies alone. That also pins the channel factors: for an all-plus
subset $k_S=\sum_{i\in S}\omega_i^2>0$, so the factor $\omega_S^2-k_S=2\,e_2(x_S)$ is abs-free; for a
type-1 subset $k_S=-\omega_\mu^2+\sum_P\omega_j^2$ has indefinite sign and $\omega_S^2-|k_S|$ carries an
absolute value. Since the hint forbids absolute values, I conjecture only all-plus channels appear.

\section*{4. Hypothesis: $A_5=N/D$ with $D$ built from all-plus channels --- fails}
For $n=5$ the all-plus channels are $\{34\},\{35\},\{45\}$ (factors $2\omega_i\omega_j$) and the full
$\{345\}$ (factor $2e_2(x)=2\omega_1\omega_2$). Their symmetric products are powers of $e_2,e_3$. I fit
$A_5=N/D$ with $N$ a generic symmetric polynomial and $D$ ranging over
$$D\in\{1,\ e_2,\ e_3,\ e_2e_3,\ e_3^2,\ e_2^2,\ e_2e_3^2,\ e_2^2e_3,\ e_3^3,\ e_2e_3^3,\ e_2^3\}.$$
Every single one is inconsistent (e.g. ``fail 226/240''). So no symmetric polynomial numerator works over
any of these denominators.

\section*{5. Hypothesis: general symmetric $N/D$ --- also fails, but the solver is fine}
I drop the assumed $D$ and solve the homogeneous system $A\cdot D-N=0$ for $N,D$ both \emph{general}
symmetric polynomials, reading the null space over $400$ exact points. For every denominator degree
$d_D=0,1,2,\dots,12$ the null space is empty (\texttt{dim}=0). To make sure the solver is not lying I feed
it a synthetic symmetric rational, e.g.
$$F=\frac{p_2(x)^3+5e_1(x)^6-3e_2(x)e_1(x)^4}{e_2(x)^2},$$
and it recovers it at exactly the right degree ($d_D=4$). So the solver works; the disturbing conclusion
is that $A_5$ is not a symmetric rational function of the plus frequencies of any low denominator degree.

\section*{6. A one-parameter slice, and the first paradox}
I reconstruct $A_5$ along $\omega_2=2,\omega_3=\tfrac52$, varying $\omega_4=t$ (with $\omega_5,\omega_1$
derived). Exact rational interpolation gives
$$A_5(t)=-256\,\frac{4t^2+18t+45}{2t+9}.$$
Sanity at $t=3$: $-256\cdot\tfrac{135}{15}=-2304$. The only pole, $t=-\tfrac92$, is where
$\omega_2+\omega_3+\omega_4=0$ (so $\omega_5\to\infty$): a parametrization artifact, not a physical
channel. So along this slice $A_5$ has \emph{no} physical pole. Computing $e_2(x)$ on the same slice gives
$-(4t^2+18t+45)/(2t+9)$, so
$$A_5(t)=256\,e_2(x)=256\,\omega_1\omega_2 \quad\text{on this slice.}$$
But $A_5$ is degree $6$ and $\omega_1\omega_2$ is degree $2$, so the ``$256$'' cannot be a constant---it
must be a degree-$4$ quantity that equals $256$ here.

\section*{7. $G=A_5/(\omega_1\omega_2)$ and the perfect powers}
I tabulate $G:=A_5/(\omega_1\omega_2)$ (degree $4$, symmetric). Fixing $\omega_2=2$ and varying:
$$\{2,\tfrac52,3\}\!\to\!256,\ \{2,\tfrac52,4\}\!\to\!256,\ \{2,\tfrac52,\tfrac72\}\!\to\!256,\
\{2,\tfrac52,\tfrac32\}\!\to\!207,\ \{2,\tfrac52,1\}\!\to\!112,\ \{2,3,4\}\!\to\!256,\ \{2,3,\tfrac32\}\!\to\!207.$$
So $G$ is $256$ widely but $207,112$ when $\omega_4$ is small. A degree-$4$ homogeneous function cannot be
constant on an open set unless globally constant, so $\{G=256\}$ is not open---there is a wall. Then,
varying $\omega_2$ as well:
$$\{2,\tfrac52,3\}\!\to\!256{=}4^4,\ \{5/2,3,4\}\!\to\!625{=}5^4,\ \{3,\tfrac72,4\}\!\to\!1296{=}6^4,\
\{7/2,4,9/2\}\!\to\!2401{=}7^4,\ \{4,9/2,5\}\!\to\!4096{=}8^4.$$
So in this regime $G=(2\,\omega_{\min})^4$ with $\omega_{\min}$ the softest leg---and the softest leg is a
minus leg in all of these. The deviations $207,112$ occur exactly when a plus leg becomes the softest. I
now recognise a chamber structure controlled by the signs of the composite $k_S$. The transition near
$\{2,5/2,\cdot\}$ is governed by $\operatorname{sign}(k_{24})=\operatorname{sign}(\omega_4^2-\omega_2^2)$: $256$ for $\omega_4>2$, then
$207$ at $\omega_4=\tfrac32$, $112$ at $\omega_4=1$. Indeed $256-G=16\,(\omega_2^2-\omega_4^2)^2$ on that
slice (for $\omega_4<\omega_2$): $\tfrac74\!\to\!49,\ 3\!\to\!144,\ \tfrac{15}{4}\!\to\!225,\dots$, i.e.
$G=16\,\omega_4^2(2\omega_2^2-\omega_4^2)$.

\section*{8. Chamber grouping --- per-chamber symmetric fit still fails}
I group points by the full sign pattern of $\{k_S\}$ and reconstruct inside one chamber. For $n=5$ I find
$16$ chambers, the largest with $703$ points; symmetric reconstruction inside it has \texttt{dim}=0 up to
$d_D=8$. The reason, once I see it, is decisive: a chamber is cut by inequalities like
$\omega_4^2\gtrless\omega_2^2$ that single out individual legs, so it is \emph{not} $S_2\times S_{n-2}$
invariant, and the per-chamber expression need not be symmetric in the plus frequencies even though the
physical value is. So my symmetric plus-frequency ansatz was the wrong object on a chamber. I confirm the
amplitude itself is symmetric: swapping $\omega_1\leftrightarrow\omega_2$ (and $k_1\leftrightarrow k_2$),
or permuting plus legs, leaves \bg{} unchanged ($-2304$ either way).

\section*{9. Symbolic chamber-resolved BG, and a stuck simplification}
I write a symbolic BG (\texttt{sbg.py}) that resolves every $|k|$ to $\pm k$ by its sign at a reference
point $(-\tfrac92,2,\tfrac52,3,-3)$. It matches $-2304\,i$ there and yields an exact off-shell rational
function whose denominator factors into a mess of off-shell artifacts---e.g.
$$w_2^3,\ (w_1\pm w_3),\ (w_2+w_3)^4,\ (w_3^2+w_4^2),\ (w_1^2-w_3^2-w_4^2)^2,\ (w_3w_4+w_3w_5+w_4w_5).$$
But reducing it onto the manifold (\texttt{sympy} \texttt{cancel}/\texttt{simplify}) times out at $300$\,s.

\section*{10. Confirming the piecewise behaviour against the reference}
Worried the chambers might be an artifact of my port, I re-check the ``deviation'' points in the supplied
Mathematica directly:
$$\{2,\tfrac52,3\}\!\to\!-2304,\ \{2,\tfrac52,\tfrac32\}\!\to\!-\tfrac{5589}{4},\
\{2,\tfrac52,1\}\!\to\!-\tfrac{7504}{11},\ \{2,3,4\}\!\to\!-\tfrac{8704}{3},\ \{3,4,5\}\!\to\!-28512.$$
The reference reproduces them exactly. The piecewise behaviour is real, and it matches the comment in
\texttt{OnShellBG.m}: ``No regularization \dots no poles in this sector.'' The propagator poles cancel; the
amplitude is bounded.

\section*{11. No real poles; continuity across a wall}
A scan over thousands of points gives $|A_5|/(\text{scale})^6\lesssim3$: no real poles. Approaching a plus
leg $\omega_4\to0$ the amplitude stays finite ($-0.628$ at $\omega_4=\tfrac1{32}$); a minus leg
$\omega_2\to0$ gives $A\to0$. Across the wall $\omega_4=\omega_2=2$ (fixing $\omega_2=2,\omega_3=\tfrac52$):
$$A(2.2)=-1986,\ A(2.1)=-1947.9,\ A(2.01)=-1913.9,\ A(2)=\text{degenerate},\ A(1.99)=-1906.2,\ A(1.9)=-1855.$$
The two sides meet ($\approx-1910$); refining one-sided slopes with step $10^{-3}$ they converge
($-375.7$ vs $-381.3$), so $A$ is continuous and nearly smooth at the wall. That briefly reopened the
single-rational hope.

\section*{12. The decisive test: $A_5=16\,\omega_1\omega_2^5$ on an open set}
On increasing-ordered positive free frequencies (so $\omega_2$ is the global softest),
$A_5=16\,\omega_1\omega_2^5$ holds at $84/84$ grid points, and continues to hold at deliberately generic,
near-equal-magnitude increasing points:
$$\{13/7,29/11,41/9\},\ \{17/8,23/7,53/10\},\ \{7/3,19/5,31/6\},\ \{11/9,101/50,73/20\},\ \{2,100/49,25/12\}.$$
This is the killer. $A_5$ equals the polynomial $16\,\omega_1\omega_2^5$ on an open set; a single rational
function equal to it there would equal it everywhere, but at $\{2,5/2,3/2\}$ it is
$-\tfrac{5589}{4}\neq16\,\omega_1\omega_2^5$. Sharper: within the softest-is-minus region, on the open
piece $\{\omega_1^2<\omega_2^2\}$ the amplitude is $16\,\omega_1^5\omega_2$, while on
$\{\omega_2^2<\omega_1^2\}$ it is the \emph{different} rational $16\,\omega_1\omega_2^5$ (later verified
$67/67$ and $233/233$). No single rational function can be two different ones on two open sets. So the
hint's premise is, for this code, false: $A_n$ is bounded and piecewise, not a single rational function.

\section*{13. The clean principal-regime law}
The polynomial $16\,\omega_1\omega_2^5$ generalises. At $n=6$ I find $A_6/(\omega_1\omega_2)=2048=2^{11}$
on $\omega_2=2$ points, i.e. $A_6=32\,\omega_1\omega_2^7$; the prefactor is $2^{n-1}$ ($16,32$) and the
exponent follows from homogeneity. Writing it symmetrically with the softer minus leg,
$$\boxed{\,A_n=i\,2^{\,n-1}\,\omega_1\omega_2\,\bigl(\min(\omega_1^2,\omega_2^2)\bigr)^{n-3}\,}\qquad
\text{whenever }\min_i\omega_i^2\text{ is a }\sigma=-1\text{ leg.}$$
This is sign-robust. A systematic scan: with $\min$ a minus leg it holds $112/112$ ($n=5$), $420/420$
($n=6$); with $\min$ a plus leg it holds $0/222$, $0/1224$ (never). On random-sign points it holds
$200/200,\ 40/40,\ 8/8$ at $n=5,6,7$. This regime contains every two-minus example in \texttt{OnShellBG.m}.

\section*{14. $n=4$ as a limit}
The same law reads $A_4=i\,8\,\omega_1\omega_2\min(\omega_1^2,\omega_2^2)$. \bg{} is $0/0$ there, but
approaching off-shell, $\omega\to(-b,a,b+\varepsilon,-a+\varepsilon)$, $\varepsilon\to0$, the limit converges to it:
$$(a,b)=(2,3),(3,5),(2,5),(4,3)\ \Rightarrow\ -192,\ -1080,\ -320,\ -864,$$
(numerically $-191.978,\dots$ at $\varepsilon=10^{-4}$). Note $n=4$ is exactly the boundary where a minus and a
plus leg are tied for softest, which is why \bg{} degenerates.

\section*{15. The rest of the sector: sorted-leg structure, with a sign subtlety}
The principal regime is a minority of generic configurations once $n\ge5$ ($n-2$ plus legs versus two
minus legs). For the plus-softest region the clean power breaks: $A_5/(\omega_1\omega_2)$ stops being a
perfect square, and a symmetric reconstruction restricted to ``softest is plus'' also fails ($\texttt{dim}=0$),
because that region is itself cut into finer chambers. Sorting all legs by $|\omega|$ as $s_0\le s_1\le\dots$
with types, I find the cases
\begin{align*}
\text{softest minus:}&\quad G=16\,s_0^4;\\
\text{softest plus, $2$nd minus:}&\quad G=16\,s_0^2(2s_1^2-s_0^2)\quad
[\{2,\tfrac52,\tfrac32\}{:}\,207,\ \{2,\tfrac52,1\}{:}\,112,\ \{3,\tfrac72,1\}{:}\,272,\ \{3,\tfrac12,\tfrac72\}{:}\,71];\\
\text{two softest plus:}&\quad G=32\,s_0^2s_1^2\quad
[\{5/2,\tfrac12,\tfrac34\}{:}\,\tfrac92,\ \{3,\tfrac13,\tfrac12\}{:}\,\tfrac89].
\end{align*}
But the naive sorted-by-magnitude formula fails $19/1500$ on fully random points, e.g. at
$\omega=(\tfrac{5116}{603},-\tfrac{27}{4},-\tfrac{28}{9},8,-\tfrac{1775}{268})$: the amplitude depends on
the \emph{signs} of the frequencies (vertices carry $\omega$ linearly), not just their magnitudes. The
min-is-minus law is special precisely in being sign-robust.

\section*{16. The global linear-$|k|$ ansatz for $n=5$ --- success}
The honest variables are the type-1 channel momenta themselves. I posit, allowing the absolute values
explicitly,
$$A_5=i\Bigl[\,P_0(\omega)+\sum_{\mu\in\{1,2\}}\sum_{j\in\{3,4,5\}}P_{\mu j}(\omega)\,\bigl|\omega_j^2-\omega_\mu^2\bigr|\Bigr],$$
with $P_0$ symmetric of degree $6$ and the coefficients symmetric under the residual symmetry; the
$|\omega_j^2-\omega_\mu^2|=|k_{\mu j}|$ are exactly the (one-minus, one-plus) channel momenta. The fit is a
single linear problem over all chambers. The augmented system is rank-deficient (rank $22$) only because of
the manifold relations, but it is \emph{consistent}---one $P_0$ and one family $P_{\mu j}$ reproduce every
chamber, $0$ mismatches. One exact representative:
$$P_0=8\,\omega_1\omega_2\,\bigl(P_4-4E_1E_3\bigr),\qquad P_4=\omega_3^4+\omega_4^4+\omega_5^4,$$
with $E_1,E_3$ the elementary symmetric functions of the plus legs, and, with $\mu'$ the other minus leg
and $e_1,e_2$ the elementary symmetric functions of the two plus legs $\neq j$,
$$P_{\mu j}=8\bigl(e_1^3\omega_{\mu'}+2e_1e_2\,\omega_j-e_1e_2\,\omega_{\mu'}-e_1\omega_{\mu'}^3+2e_2^2+e_2\omega_{\mu'}^2\bigr).$$
Verified at $800$ random points spanning all chambers (the softest leg observed to be each of the five legs
in turn): $0$ mismatches, max relative error $0$. So the absolute values the hint forbade are essential and
unavoidable---they carry the chamber structure---and once admitted, the amplitude \emph{is} a single global
expression.

\section*{17. $n=6$ needs products of $|k|$; the general boundary laws}
The same linear-in-$|k|$ ansatz is \emph{inconsistent} at $n=6$ (rank $54$). The resolution is that $n=6$
needs \emph{products} of $|k_S|$ (the formula is multilinear in the type-1 momenta), reflecting the $n-3$
nested soft channels, with $n=5$ being the lucky case needing only one factor. The clean limits survive
and corroborate this. When the $n-3$ softest legs are all $\sigma=+1$,
$$A_n=i\,2^{\,n-1}(n-3)!\,\omega_1\omega_2\!\!\prod_{\text{softest }n-3\text{ plus}}\!\!\omega_j^2,$$
verified e.g. at $n=6$ for $\{3,\tfrac12,\tfrac34,\tfrac54\}$ giving $H=\tfrac{675}{512}=6\prod e_i$
(the factorial $6=(n-3)!$ being the signature of a sum over orderings of the soft channels); and the
soft-minus end gives the $(\min(\omega_1^2,\omega_2^2))^{n-3}$ law. The mixed $n=6$ cases
($\{2,\tfrac52,3,1\}{:}\,H=37$, $\{3,\tfrac72,1,\tfrac34\}{:}\,H=\tfrac{7101}{256}$) interpolate between
these and require the full multilinear structure. I extracted the explicit complete form only for $n=5$;
for $n\ge6$ I leave the explicit principal/all-plus boundary laws plus the multilinear structural statement
rather than dress up the $n=5$ result as more than it is.

\section*{18. The picture, and what was verified}
In this sector the would-be propagator poles $\omega_S^2=|k_S|$ never produce a pole of the assembled
amplitude (they cancel), so $A_n$ is bounded and equals, on each chamber, a polynomial of degree $2(n-2)$.
The chambers are the sign patterns of the type-1 sub-energies $k_S=\sum_{i\in S}\sigma_i\omega_i^2$; the
all-plus channels are positive and contribute nothing piecewise. The amplitude is dominated by the softest
legs, the softest minus leg acting as a cap (the clean power law) and soft plus legs contributing the
nested $|k_{\mu j}|$ structure. All claims are checked to the last digit in exact rational arithmetic
against the supplied \bg{}: the exact BG-port match; degree $2(n-2)$; the not-a-single-rational proof
($67/67$ and $233/233$); the principal law at $n=4$ (limit), $5,6,7,8$ (e.g. $n=8$:
$\{3/2,2,5/2,3,7/2,4\}\to-\tfrac{37496115}{352}\,i$ and $\{2,5/2,3,7/2,4,9/2\}\to-\tfrac{115343360}{39}\,i$);
and the complete $n=5$ formula at $300$--$800$ random points across all chambers.
